patterns_data.top_pattern: VA acute hospital spend surged across Medicare products, led by DSNP admissions and a few major hospital systems
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: VA / ACUTE HOSPITAL / DSNP HMO, CSNP HMO, Medicare HMO
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA acute hospital costs increased across multiple Medicare products, with DSNP HMO driving most of the spend and CSNP HMO and Medicare HMO adding further volume. The main story is more admissions, but a smaller provider-specific cost layer is also present, especially at Sentara Norfolk General. This is a concentrated hospital-market pattern rather than a broad statewide price issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the largest real utilization-driven cost increase in the analysis and is concentrated enough to support targeted provider and UM action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open a joint VA acute hospital action plan across UM and network teams focused on the named hospitals, using admission growth as the lead issue and provider-specific payment variance as a secondary workstream.
evidence_summary: VA DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased by about $64.3M, with 4,194 more admissions and about $879 higher paid per admit.
VA CSNP HMO acute hospital spend added about $10.4M on 771 more admissions, even though paid per admit fell by about $1,943.
VA Medicare HMO acute hospital spend added about $7.7M on 415 more admissions.
Sentara Norfolk General added about $4.9M in VA DSNP acute hospital spend with 257 more admissions and about $1,038 higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.top_pattern: VA authorization classification shifted enough to block clean business action
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA shows a very large movement in authorization classification rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement signal. The shift is widespread enough to affect the same hospitals showing major spend growth. Business action on authorization performance, denial policy, or provider behavior should wait until this classification movement is confirmed.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the authorization flag moved, leaders could misread operational performance and take the wrong action on a very large dollar base.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have UM operations and data quality teams reconcile how authorization status is populated for VA claims and authorizations, then restate the affected reporting before changing policy or provider management.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is explicitly flagged as an authorization or mapping shift that requires validation before action.
evidence_summary: VA authorization classification movement totals about $62.8M at the state level.
VCU Medical Center accounts for about $5.5M of the shift.
Sentara Leigh Hospital accounts for about $2.6M and Carilion Roanoke Memorial Hospital about $1.4M.
The same providers also appear in the major VA acute hospital cost patterns, increasing the risk of misattribution if the flag is wrong.

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX acute hospital spend increased first because DSNP HMO admissions grew statewide, and second because Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital showed materially higher paid per admit in both DSNP HMO and Medicare HMO. patterns_data.why_it_matters: TX is the second-largest operational cost story and includes a clear named-hospital lever for network and payment action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Pair UM review of rising TX acute admissions with a focused financial review of Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital covering pricing, billing, and payment accuracy across DSNP HMO and Medicare HMO.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased by about $48.5M with 2,233 more admissions and about $413 higher paid per admit.
Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital added about $6.9M in TX DSNP acute hospital spend with 338 more admissions and about $4,973 higher paid per admit.
The same hospital added about $3.6M in TX Medicare HMO acute hospital spend with 159 more admissions and about $7,918 higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of DSNP cost movement in TX and a smaller pocket in LA is landing in a Not Mapped facility bucket. That prevents clean site-of-care, provider mix, and authorization interpretation because the claims cannot be reliably assigned to the right facility type. This needs to be fixed before the business treats the pattern as true utilization or unit-cost change.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If facility mapping is wrong, site-of-care strategy and provider accountability will be misdirected.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Correct the facility mapping for Not Mapped DSNP claims in TX and LA, then rebuild the affected site-of-care and authorization reporting before taking provider or UM action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The claims are explicitly concentrated in a Not Mapped facility bucket, so business interpretation is not reliable until classification is corrected.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO Not Mapped facility claims increased by about $8.5M with 214 more admissions and about $27.9K higher paid per admit.

LA DSNP HMO Not Mapped facility claims added about $283K with 23 more admissions, but paid per admit fell by about $26.8K, which is more consistent with classification noise than a stable site-of-care trend.

These are better managed as local validation and provider triage items than enterprise-wide strategy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These pockets should not distract from the main VA and TX levers, but they still warrant local cleanup so they do not become repeat drivers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Assign local market owners to validate the small concentrated pockets, confirm authorization and site-of-care coding, and only escalate markets that continue to grow after cleanup.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Most of these pockets are low-volume, concentrated, or include explicit authorization and mapping anomalies, which limits confidence for broad action.

OH authorization classification movement totals about $363K and is concentrated in Osteomyelitis with CC and Postoperative and Posttraumatic Infections without MCC.
NJ, NY, and OH DSNP HMO free-standing SNF pressure totals about $276K and is low-volume.
CA and IN acute hospital pockets total about $147K, and the FL LTCH pocket is a single-case level issue at about $36K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Small but recurring high-cost infection, sepsis, and musculoskeletal episodes need targeted clinical review, not broad policy changes
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: TX, VA, and OH / IP Med/Surg and NF focused high-cost cases
key_driver_codes: Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
Amputation for Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue Disorders with CC
Postoperative and Posttraumatic Infections without MCC
Bone Diseases and Arthropathies with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Clinical outliers are recurring across TX, VA, and OH, but they are concentrated in small pockets rather than broad population shifts. The most common themes are sepsis, osteomyelitis, amputation-related complications, postoperative infection, and musculoskeletal NF cases. Because many are low-baseline or small-count episodes, the right action is targeted chart, coding, and care-path review at the case or provider level.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These cases can be clinically important and costly, but they are too concentrated for broad utilization or benefit changes without validation.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send these cases to clinical and coding review to confirm diagnosis accuracy, acuity, and post-acute placement need, then decide whether any targeted provider or care-management intervention is warranted.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Many of the clinical groups are flagged as low baseline or small-count events, so chart and coding confirmation is needed before broader action.
evidence_summary: At Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital in TX, sepsis cases added about $539K with 31 more admissions and about $17.4K higher paid per admit.
At Sentara Leigh Hospital in VA, sepsis cases added about $515K with 36 more admissions.
VA NF musculoskeletal and osteomyelitis-related case mix totals about $0.8M across osteoarthritis and osteomyelitis diagnoses.
OH and TX rare IP Med/Surg infection and amputation-related pockets add about $377K and are mostly one- or two-admission events.

summary_table.subtitle: Small but recurring high-cost infection, sepsis, and musculoskeletal episodes need targeted clinical review, not broad policy changes

rows.clinical_review_rules: Requires sepsis evidence, supporting documentation, appropriate treatment, and correct infection-first code sequencing.
Requires documented sepsis with organ dysfunction, SOFA ≥2, and treatment; excludes SIRS/SEP-1/qSOFA.
Requires covered diagnosis; ESR not reimbursed when billed with CRP tests.
Requires Sepsis-3/SOFA ≥2 documentation supporting sepsis diagnosis and related treatment services.
Requires documentation supporting sepsis-related services per Sepsis-3 with SOFA score ≥2.
Enforces correct principal diagnosis and ICD-10-CM sequencing, manifestation, code-first, sequela, and Excludes1 rules.
